title: Existence of Cartan--Eilenberg injective resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives], and let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex in $\mathcal B$ with $K^p=0$ for $p<0$. There exists a first-quadrant double complex $I^{p,q}$ [def-sp-double-complex-total] with an augmentation $K^\bullet\to I^{\bullet,0}$ such that each column $I^{p,\bullet}$ is an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $K^p$. In every fixed resolution degree $q$, the horizontal cycles $\ker(d_I:I^{p,q}\to I^{p+1,q})$, boundaries $\operatorname{im}(d_I:I^{p-1,q}\to I^{p,q})$, and cohomology objects $H^p_I(I^{\bullet,q})$ are injective. For each $p$, their complexes in the resolution degree $q$ are injective resolutions of $Z^p(K^\bullet)$, $B^p(K^\bullet)$, and $H^p(K^\bullet)$, respectively. This double complex is a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution of $K^\bullet$.

proof.text: Use the given bound with $n=0$, and put $Z^p=\ker(d_K^p)$, $B^p=\operatorname{im}(d_K^{p-1})$, and $H^p=Z^p/B^p$. Exactness of kernels, images, and cokernels in the abelian category gives the alternating short exact sequences $0\to Z^0\to K^0\to B^1\to0$, $0\to B^1\to Z^1\to H^1\to0$, and the analogous pair in every later degree.

source.place: Lemma 015I (lemma-cartan-eilenberg), proof: decomposition into the alternating short exact sequences

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $Z^0\to J_Z^{0,\bullet}$ with $J_Z^{0,q}=0$ for $q<0$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1). Apply the horseshoe lemma with prescribed end resolutions [lem-sp-horseshoe-prescribed-resolutions] to $0\to Z^0\to K^0\to B^1\to0$, with the given resolution $J_Z^{0,\bullet}$ of $Z^0$ and any injective resolution of $B^1$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1); it yields an injective resolution $K^0\to I^{0,\bullet}$ and a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to J_Z^{0,\bullet}\to I^{0,\bullet}\to J_B^{1,\bullet}\to0$ of complexes compatible with the augmentations, in which the outer complexes are the prescribed ones. Apply the same lemma to $0\to B^1\to Z^1\to H^1\to0$ with the resolution $J_B^{1,\bullet}$ just obtained (and any resolution of $H^1$), giving $0\to J_B^{1,\bullet}\to J_Z^{1,\bullet}\to J_H^{1,\bullet}\to0$; then to $0\to Z^1\to K^1\to B^2\to0$ with this $J_Z^{1,\bullet}$, and so on inductively through all degrees. Prescribing the subobject resolution is what makes consecutive rows share $J_B^{p+1,\bullet}$ and $J_Z^{p,\bullet}$. Put $J_B^{0,\bullet}=0$ and $J_H^{0,\bullet}=J_Z^{0,\bullet}$ (as $B^0=0$, $H^0=Z^0$). All complexes vanish in negative resolution degrees.

source.place: Lemma 015I (lemma-cartan-eilenberg), proof Steps 1-4, using Lemma 013T (in its 'given injective resolutions' form)

proof.text: Let $I^{p,\bullet}$ be the resolution of $K^p$ produced at the $p$-th stage. Define the horizontal differential $d_I:I^{p,\bullet}\to I^{p+1,\bullet}$ as the composite $I^{p,\bullet}\to J_B^{p+1,\bullet}\to J_Z^{p+1,\bullet}\to I^{p+1,\bullet}$ through the quotient and subobject resolutions supplied by the two adjacent horseshoe rows [lem-sp-horseshoe-prescribed-resolutions]. The compatibility in the horseshoe diagrams makes these maps commute with vertical differentials and induces $d_K$ on the augmentations; exactness of the rows gives $d_I d_I=0$.

source.place: Lemma 015I (lemma-cartan-eilenberg), proof conclusion: define d_1 by the composite through J_B and J_Z

proof.text: The construction is zero for horizontal degree $p<0$ (we started at $n=0$) and for resolution degree $q<0$, so it is first quadrant. Each vertical column resolves $K^p$ by construction. In each fixed $q$, exactness of the two adjacent horseshoe rows [lem-sp-horseshoe-prescribed-resolutions] (the composite $J_B^{p+1,q}\to J_Z^{p+1,q}\to I^{p+1,q}$ is monic and $I^{p,q}\to J_B^{p+1,q}$ is epic) identifies the horizontal cycles with the chosen injective resolution of $Z^p(K)$, the horizontal boundaries with that of $B^p(K)$, and horizontal cohomology with that of $H^p(K)$; all terms are injective and the augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms. Thus the stated Cartan--Eilenberg conditions hold.

lean.statement: theorem exists_cartanEilenberg_resolution (B : Type u) [Category.{v} B] [Abelian B] [EnoughInjectives B] (K : CochainComplex B ℤ) (hK : ∀ p : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (K.X p)) : ∃ (I : HomologicalComplex₂ B (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ)) (e : ((CochainComplex.single₀ B).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K ⟶ I), (∀ p : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero (I.X p)) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso (e.f p)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ), Injective ((I.X p).X q)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ), Injective ((I.cycles p).X q) ∧ Injective ((image (I.d (p - 1) p)).X q) ∧ Injective ((I.homology p).X q)) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.cyclesMap e p) ∧ QuasiIso (image.map (Arrow.homMk' (e.f (p - 1)) (e.f p) (e.comm (p - 1) p))) ∧ QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap e p))
lean.note: Uses the dependency-recorded Mathlib bicomplex and homology declarations. The natural vertical index is the nonnegative restriction, extended by zero in negative degrees. InjectiveResolution is expressed by its defining fields: degreewise injectivity and a quasi-isomorphism from an object in degree zero. All four augmentations arise from the same bicomplex morphism.
